current.text: He has a hamstring injury and will miss the preseason. He will be re-evaluated in week one and might miss one or two games, or none. Yahoo lists him as questionable.
LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are gone from Charlotte. He is a projected starter with Coby White, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté. Grayson Allen starts while he is out.
His usage should rise from 22% to about 24 or 25%. Expect more shots and more turnovers.

He is a candidate to take on more of the creation load. One expert expects him to create more than Brandon Miller and calls him a good passer. How White, Knueppel and Miller will split the ball handling is still an open question.
Experts expect his shooting efficiency to drop without LaMelo Ball's passing. That could cancel out gains in points and assists, and he may not beat last season's category rank.

Experts say he is heavily overdrafted. They value him in the 60s to 70s and say not to take him in the top 50 or in rounds 3 or 4. One expert says the 50s are acceptable, and another would take him around ESPN rank 91.
In a mock auction, Josh would not go above 8 USD for him. He sold for 13 USD, which Josh called too much.
With a March 28 end date, Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. The team has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte's two-game week starting March 1 should not factor into decisions about him.
Charlotte is leaning fully into spacing the floor and will take a lot of threes.
Playmaking in Charlotte is expected to be spread across several players, with no single primary creator.

durable.text: Threes are his standout category. His three-point volume is far above the top 250 pool, and he shot 42% from three as a rookie.
He does little beyond points and threes. He gets few steals and blocks and is not a big rebounder.
His shooting was great overall but clearly worse when he played without LaMelo Ball.
As a rookie he finished 66th in category leagues but ranked only 91st over the final two months.
His late fade looked like a partial rookie wall.
His game is not particularly friendly to points leagues. He has been worth more in 9-cat (66th) than in points (89th).

note: He costs about 16 USD at Yahoo (rank 64) and 15 USD at ESPN (rank 39). Experts value him in the 60s to 70s, and in one mock auction Josh would pay no more than 8 USD, so our room will likely overpay. He is a 3PM specialist with no category flagged weak, so he fits most builds as a threes and points source, but his low steals and blocks cap his value. Early in the season, check the hamstring at the week-one re-evaluation and whether his FG% holds up without LaMelo Ball. If it does not, his rookie efficiency will not carry over.
